observed-problem: Tests derived from the implementation can pass despite a disconnected consumer or wrong output contract.
proposed-rule: Choose independent expected behavior and verify the relevant consumer path.
expected-result: Checks reject wrong behavior and disconnected implementation without redundant tests.
rollback: Revert this isolated patch and regenerate projections with the same pinned generator.
composition: Test separately before combining; shared catalog edits require a newly declared combined delta.
problem-provenance: Protective procedure proposed in the approved plan; no live failure is attributed to the original Core without matched evidence.
projection-evidence-boundary: Deterministic representation only; no useful activation or behavioral benefit is established.
coverage-boundary: Trusted static literal assertions at the public consumer against accepted samples; specified identity and wrong-delta mutations. No fixture execution, actual runtime/test-run result or independent model reasoning is proved. Finite observer metrics remain emitted-output proxies.
decision-boundary: R31 is a completed but unqualified baseline. Limited control adequacy and unsupported output/source grammar prevent broad Core conclusions. No historical regrading, selective retry or cost compensation. Changed instrumentation requires a newly declared baseline, not an exception to promotion gates.
